//: Gzipped ceilings for every published bundle, in bytes. Read by scripts/check-size.mjs in CI. Raising a number is a deliberate edit with a reason in the commit message, not silent drift. The core ceiling is set so the documented '~10kb' stays true: 10600 bytes is 10.4KB, which rounds to 10; past 10751 the claim needs rewording, not just a bigger budget. Raised from 9600 (under '~9kb') when error diagnostics landed and crossed that line on its own, then from 10400 to 10600 when four bug fixes together came to 10406, leaving room for the queued devtools plugins view (+132). Raised to 10700 for the core audit fixes (ISSUE-0045 to ISSUE-0050), about 45 bytes across three PRs: v-show showing an element that starts with display: none, v-model leaving an unset field empty, nested v-once, v-bind keeping static class and style, invalid markup selectors reported instead of thrown, and the root $watch stopping on unmount. That left no headroom at 10600. Headroom is a few percent by design — enough that ordinary work does not trip it, tight enough that a real feature is a conversation.
//plugins: morph raised from 1400 to 1450, and the combined plugins bundle from 4400 to 4450, when morph learned to release scope roots it removes outside every mounted scope (ISSUE-0032): about 40 bytes, and the alternative was leaking effects, listeners and devtools entries. navigate raised from 1900 to 2100 when it learned to merge the head (US-0033): 186 bytes, and without it a page-specific stylesheet never loaded after navigating. Raised again to 2250 for the audit fixes (ISSUE-0034): manual scroll restoration, the saved position over the hash, one POST per form at a time, autofocus, and keeping a stylesheet's own onload; 89 bytes. Raised to 2350 for the loading state (US-0034): aria-busy on the document and the submitting form while a navigation is in flight, handed over between overlapping navigations; 84 bytes. Raised to 2600 for opt-in prefetch (US-0034): fetching a link on hover, focus or pointerdown and handing the response to the click; about 210 bytes, and without it every click waits for the full round trip. popover raised from 1100 to 1150 when v-anchor learned to share a trigger's anchor-name (ISSUE-0035): 27 bytes, and without it a second element anchored to the same trigger lost its anchor. The combined plugins bundle raised from 4450 to 4500 when media capped its raw query subscriptions (ISSUE-0033): 27 bytes, and without it a query built from a changing value kept one MediaQueryList per value for the page's life. Raised to 4550 when v-trap learned to count only what Tab reaches (ISSUE-0038): 73 bytes, and without it a hidden input or a display: none button at the end of a dialog let Tab leave the trap. Raised to 4600 for three plugin fixes (ISSUE-0039, ISSUE-0040, ISSUE-0041): v-collapse hiding collapsed content from Tab and screen readers, v-transition keeping an inline display and removing its classes on teardown, and v-intersect acting on state changes so .leave and .full run when they say; 64 bytes. mask raised from 470 to 500, and the combined plugins bundle to 4700, when v-mask learned to format v-model's initial value and keep the caret in place (ISSUE-0042): 73 bytes, and without it a prefilled field showed its raw value and an edit in the middle threw the caret to the end. Raised again to 1175 when v-anchor positioned elements that are not popovers absolutely (ISSUE-0037): 24 bytes, and with position: fixed such an element was misplaced after any layout while its anchor was scrolled away.
//devtools: The devtools ceiling is looser than the others on purpose. This bundle is development-only and never loads in production, so its bytes cost a visitor nothing — and the panel's usability is the entire reason it exists. Raised from 5600 to 6000 when docking landed, from 6000 to 6500 when state search and a collapsible scope tree landed, from 6500 to 6800 for per-mode resize handles, and from 6800 to 7200 for the plugins view, to leave room for the panel to keep improving rather than making every UI change a budget negotiation.
